artworks.title: Laomedon Refusing Payment to Poseidon and Apollo
artworks.description: Baroque canvas of the Trojan king stiff-necked before the gods who built his walls: Poseidon and Apollo stand unpaid while Laomedon’s court watches the perjury that will bring Heracles’ sack of Troy. The painting isolates the cheat that defines Laomedon in Apollodorus and the Iliadic backstory.

artworks.title: Heracles and Laomedon
artworks.description: A Valle Sabbia museum panel stages Heracles confronting Troy’s king — the sequel to the unpaid walls and the Hesione bargain. Laomedon appears as the mortal who cheats gods and heroes alike until the city falls the first time.

music.title: Hésione
music.description: Campra’s tragédie en musique for the Paris Opéra turns on Laomedon’s Troy and the rescue of Hesione — the Trojan king’s household as French Baroque spectacle.

popCulture.title: Laomedon
popCulture.description: Trojan king, son of Ilus — the cheat who refused Poseidon and Apollo their wage and lost Hesione to Heracles’ siege.
